title: Java Particle System Editor
description: I built a Java/Swing particle-system editor as part of the internal Essential Skills training course I used with junior developers. The project taught object-oriented design, Swing/AWT GUI development, and how to build reusable visual effects that could be adapted into creative animations and rewards for children's educational software.

sections.title: Built as a Teaching Tool
paragraphs: I created the particle editor as part of the internal programming course I used to train junior developers at Essential Skills.
The goal was not just to teach Java syntax. The project gave developers a concrete visual system where they could practice object-oriented design while immediately seeing the results of their code.

sections.title: Object-Oriented Design
paragraphs: The particle system was structured around reusable objects and configurable behaviors, making it a practical way to teach encapsulation, composition, state, and interaction between classes.

sections.title: Swing & AWT GUI Development
paragraphs: The project also taught developers how to construct real desktop tooling with Java Swing and AWT rather than limiting training exercises to console applications.
The editor used GUI controls to change particle-system properties while displaying the resulting effect visually.

sections.title: Live Visual Experimentation
paragraphs: The editor provided a visual environment for experimenting with particle effects and animation parameters. Developers could change settings and immediately see how those values affected the resulting motion and appearance.

sections.title: Educational Software Connection
paragraphs: The larger teaching goal was to show junior programmers how the same programming techniques could be used to create engaging visual feedback for children's software.
Particle effects and related animation techniques were useful for activity rewards and other lightweight visual effects in the Essential Skills product suite.

sections.title: Used in Junior Developer Training
paragraphs: This was not merely an example I prepared and discarded. I used this exact project as part of the training material for junior developers over many years.

historicalNotes: The particle editor was used approximately from 2000 through 2010 as part of Jamie's internal Essential Skills junior-developer training course.
It was a solo-developed Java/Swing/AWT project.
Its main purpose was teaching object-oriented programming, Swing/AWT development, and the creation of visual animations for children's educational software.
Jamie used this exact project with junior developers rather than only teaching similar concepts abstractly.
Particle-style effects and related techniques were also useful for visual rewards and animations inside Essential Skills activities.
The original portfolio card describes the project as a GUI-based particle editor created to strengthen OOP using Swing and later used to teach junior programmers Object Oriented Design.
